title: Java Enums
learningObjectives: Explain an enum as a type with a fixed set of named constants.
Declare an enum and use its constants.
Use enum values in switch statements.
Call values and valueOf on an enum type.
Explain enum constants, values and valueOf, and initialize per-constant data through enum constructors.

understand.concept: An enum defines a type whose possible values are a fixed set of named constants. Enum constants are instances of the enum type. Enums improve readability and type safety compared with representing a fixed set of choices using arbitrary strings or integers.
understand.whyItMatters: Enums make allowed choices explicit and help prevent invalid values. They are useful for statuses, directions, categories and other small, stable sets of alternatives.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Enum types and constants

An enum declares a fixed set of named instances. Declare constants separated by commas and refer to them with the enum type, such as `Day.MONDAY`. Enums provide type safety compared with representing a fixed set of choices as arbitrary strings or integers.

## Built-in enum operations

Every enum provides `values()`, which returns its constants in declaration order, and `valueOf(String)`, which looks up a constant by its exact declared name. An unknown or incorrectly cased name causes IllegalArgumentException. Enums can be used in switch statements and expressions.

## Fields, constructors and methods

An enum may store data for each constant and expose it through methods. Declare fields, then list constants with constructor arguments, followed by a constructor and accessors. Enum constructors are implicitly private; they cannot be public or protected, and callers cannot instantiate enum values with `new`.

## Example design

A Priority enum can associate LOW, NORMAL and HIGH with numeric levels. Each constant supplies its level in the declaration, the constructor stores it in a final field, and an accessor returns it. This keeps the label and its associated data together.

## Common mistakes

- Treating an enum constant as an arbitrary String.
- Passing a name to valueOf with the wrong spelling or case.
- Assuming values() returns constants in alphabetical order rather than declaration order.
- Attempting to call an enum constructor directly.
- Exposing mutable state from an enum when a final field is sufficient.

examples.title: Declare and print an enum
examples.code:
enum Level { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Level current = Level.MEDIUM; System.out.println(current); } }
examples.explanation: The variable can hold one of the declared Level constants.

examples.title: Use enum in a switch
examples.code:
enum Signal { RED, GREEN }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Signal s = Signal.GREEN; switch (s) { case RED -> System.out.println("Stop"); case GREEN -> System.out.println("Go"); } } }
examples.explanation: Switch selects a branch based on the enum constant.

examples.title: List enum constants
examples.code:
enum Size { SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { for (Size s : Size.values()) System.out.println(s); } }
examples.explanation: values() returns the constants in declaration order.

examples.title: Look up a constant by name
examples.code:
enum Direction { NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Direction d = Direction.valueOf("WEST"); System.out.println(d); } }
examples.explanation: valueOf matches the exact enum constant name.

examples.title: Enum constants with constructor data
examples.explanation: Each enum constant passes arguments to its enum constructor. The constructor stores values in final fields, and accessor methods expose those values.

practise.guidedTask: Define an enum Priority with LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH constants. Give each constant an integer level through a constructor and method, then print each name and level using values(). Explain why enum constructors cannot be called with new.
practise.independentTask: Create an OrderStatus enum with a descriptive label and a boolean terminal flag. Use a switch expression to produce a message for each status, and test all constants.
hints: Enum constants are the only instances declared by the enum; use the type name to refer to each constant.
values returns constants in declaration order, while valueOf requires an exact constant name and can throw IllegalArgumentException.
Give enum constants constructor arguments to associate data with each constant; enum constructors are implicitly private and cannot be called with new.
practise.challenge: Explain how enum constructors initialize constant-specific data. Include a test using valueOf with exact case and describe the exception raised for an unknown constant name.

questions.answer: A type with a fixed set of named constants
options: A type with a fixed set of named constants
A method with no return type
questions.explanation: Enums define a finite set of valid values.

questions.prompt: Which method returns all constants of an enum?
questions.explanation: The compiler provides a static values method for each enum.
valueOf looks up a constant by its exact declared name.

questions.prompt: Can enum constants be created using new?
questions.explanation: Enum instances are defined by the enum constants.

questions.prompt: How are enum constructor arguments supplied?
options: By calling new on the enum
By a public setter after construction
questions.explanation: Enum constants are declared with constructor arguments in the enum body.
